mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% despite the tight labor market, indicating that the Fed will not feel compelled to tighten policy aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market remains resilient despite the supply shock, with S&P 500 returns > 0 in > 60% of 60-day windows following the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns remain positive in > 50% of 20-day windows following a fed funds rate above 4%, indicating that the restrictive policy has not derailed the equity rally.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month change > 10%), it signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing market strength fails to translate into broader consumer spending growth (real PCE growth < 2% over the next 2 quarters), negating the positive equity market impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < 100k), it signals a weakening labor market that will slow consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market shrugs off the labor market weakness, with S&P 500 returns > 0 in > 60% of 20-day windows following the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and the unemployment rate both rise simultaneously, it signals a toxic combination of tightening monetary policy and labor market slack that will depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market remains resilient despite the toxic combo, with S&P 500 returns > 0 in > 50% of 60-day windows following the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending growth accelerates (3-month change > 5%) and the unemployment rate is low (< 5%), it signals a consumer-led growth surge that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer spending surge fails to boost corporate earnings (S&P 500 EPS growth < 5% over the next 2 quarters), negating the positive equity market impulse.
